events.headline: Wall Street posted its strongest session since April on Nov 9 (Dow +2.15%, S&P 500 +2.35%, Nasdaq +2.74%), led by a sharp rebound in technology names, while the VIX fell 22% to 19.92 -- its lowest close since the post-election rally -- as prior-week AI-valuation/bubble jitters eased heading into Nov 10's CPI print

Brent crude slid below $92/bbl (roughly 91.5, with some feeds showing a sharper intraday drop) on Nov 10 on Middle East peace hopes easing the geopolitical risk premium in oil, continuing last week's pullback from the Nov 3 highs near $103

China's one-year suspension of its expanded Oct 2025 rare-earth/lithium-battery export controls (MOFCOM Announcement No. 70 of 2025) was due to lapse exactly Nov 10, 2026; multiple trade-press and law-firm sources (SMM, Mining.com, Tom's Hardware, Clark Hill) report it was extended to Jan 10, 2027 following the Trump-Xi summit, though no primary MOFCOM notice was directly verified -- treated as probable but not fully confirmed

Markets await the Oct CPI report due Nov 10 (headline expected +0.3% m/m, slowing from Sept's +0.6%); Fed Governor Waller has signaled he leans toward supporting a rate hike at the December meeting, keeping financials exposed to hawkish-surprise risk this week
